correctness.rationale: Legendre yields the exact q-adic valuation s_q((q-1)2^e)/(q-1). For t=1, Lucas parity and the overlapping bit of q and q(q-1) at h=nu_2(q-1) force the left-hand binomial even while q^n is odd. If q>2^e the digit sum is exactly q-1, giving a contradiction. Thus t>=2, q<2^e, and t has the explicit finite digit bound. Direct exact binomial residues for every possible e<=4 candidate give the claimed fibers; verifier independently checks all candidates and full modulus.

value.rationale: Fixing nu_2(n) while varying both an odd prime base q and exponent t is an infinite natural subproblem of a 2026 studied prime-base binomial congruence. The proof extracts an effective finiteness bound q<2^e and an exact digit-sum bound on t, a structural obstruction special to the binary cofactor; it additionally resolves the first four dyadic valuation fibers completely. Known individual OEIS examples are not the contribution. This is a motivated local restriction on potential infinite families, not an arbitrary finite computation or a restatement of the known n=q^t p theorem.
